'''Kamo Shrine''' (鴨神社) is a {{ill|Setsumatsusha|en|Setsumatsusha|qid=Q1071160|lt=sessha}} of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|abstract|Q11581011|ja|皇大神宮|tok|tomo sewi suli Naku|zh|皇大神宮|qid=Q11581011}} ({{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|abstract|Q687168|ar|ضريح إيسه|ca|Santuari d'Ise|cs|Svatyně Ise|de|Ise-jingū|el|Μεγάλο Ιερό της Ίσε|eo|Ise-Sanktejo|es|Santuario de Ise|eu|Ise santutegi handia|fa|معبد ایسه|fi|Ise-jingū|fr|Sanctuaire d'Ise|he|מקדש איסה|hu|Iszei nagyszentély|id|Kuil Besar Ise|it|Santuario di Ise|ja|伊勢神宮|ka|ისე-ძინგუ|ko|이세 신궁|ky|Исе ибадатканасы|la|Ise Magnum Templum|lfn|Santeria de Ise|lv|Ises svētnīca|min|Kuil Gadang Ise|ml|ഐസ് ഗ്രാൻഡ് ക്ഷേത്രം|nl|Ise Jingu|no|Ise Jingū|or|ଇଶେ ମହାଶାଳ|pl|Ise-jingū|pt|Santuário de Ise|ru|Храм Исэ|sh|Veliko svetište Ise|simple|Ise Grand Shrine|sl|Veliko svetišče Ise|sv|Ise Jingū|th|ศาลเจ้าอิเซะ|tok|tomo sewi suli Ise|tr|Ise Tapınağı|uk|Святилище Ісе|vi|Thần cung Ise|zh|伊势神宫|zh_min_nan|Ise Sîn-kiong|qid=Q687168|lt=Ise Grand Shrine}}) (Inner Shrine). It is located on the mid-slope of {{ill|Mount Dainichi|ja|大日山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Dainichi (Ise)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11435625}}, and is considered the most challenging {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} to reach among the {{ill|List of Shikinaisha in Ise Province|ja|神宮125社|lt=125 Shrines of Ise}}<ref name="gk">{{ill|Gakken Plus Co., Ltd.|ja|学研パブリッシング|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gakken Publishing|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to Gakken|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q86741099}} (2013): p.69</ref>.

== Overview ==
{{ill|Kamo shrines|ja|鴨神社|lt=Kamo Shrine}} is located at 1398 Okatani, Yamaga, Tamaki Town, Watarai District, Mie Prefecture<ref name="sk1">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.201</ref>. It is one of the 13 auxiliary and subordinate shrines of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|abstract|Q11581011|ja|皇大神宮|tok|tomo sewi suli Naku|zh|皇大神宮|qid=Q11581011}} (Inner Shrine) located in Tamaki Town and Ranks 4th among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the Inner Shrine<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): pp.9–11</ref>.

The "Kamo" in the shrine name was traditionally believed to refer to an old place name. However, archaeological progress at the {{ill|Saikū|en|Saikū|qid=Q150845|lt=Saikū}} site has led to suggestions of a connection with the {{ill|Kamo clan|ja|賀茂氏}}, who served as water administrators<ref name="sk9">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.199</ref>.

The shrine grounds cover an area of 15,018 m²<ref name="sk2">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.202</ref>. The shrine building is constructed in the {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|en|Shinmei-zukuri|qid=Q930545|lt=Shinmei-zukuri}} style with a wooden plank roof, facing south, and is enclosed by a single layer of {{ill|Sacred fences|en|Tamagaki|qid=Q3078312|lt=Tamagaki}}<ref name="sk2"/>. It features one {{ill|Torii|ja|神明鳥居|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinmei torii|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 鳥居|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q234731}}<ref name="sk2"/>. The sacred object (shintai) is a stone<ref>Kaneko (1983): p.59</ref>. There is no offertory box.

A stream flowing beneath the shrine grounds is said to have never dried up, even during droughts<ref name="ic">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.65</ref>. The trees on the grounds display beautiful autumn foliage during late autumn<ref name="ic"/>.

== Enshrined Deities ==
The enshrined deities are '''Ishikorowake no Mikoto''' (石己呂和居命) and '''Mimae no Kami''' (御前神)<ref name="gk"/><ref name="ic"/>. Both deities are children of {{ill|Ōminakami no Mikoto|ja|大水上命}} and are considered gods of agriculture and irrigation<ref name="gk"/><ref name="ic"/>. Originally, there were separate shrine buildings for each deity<ref name="uy">Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.10</ref>, but after the shrine was restored by {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長}} during the Edo period, the deities have been enshrined together in a single structure<ref name="sk2"/>.

== History ==
According to the ''Enryaku Gishiki-chō'', the shrine was established during the reign of {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|es|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|fa|یاماتوهیمه نو میکوتو|fr|Yamatohime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|mni|ꯌꯃꯇꯣꯍꯤꯃꯦ-ꯅꯣ-ꯃꯤꯀꯣꯇꯣ|vi|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|zh|倭姬命|qid=Q4388732|lt=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}}<ref>Kaneko (1983): p.68</ref>, giving it a history as long as the Ise Grand Shrine itself<ref name="sk0">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.200</ref>. In ancient texts, the shrine is referred to as "Kamo-sha" or "Kamo Jinja," and its reading as "Kamo" is undisputed<ref name="sk9"/>.

It was designated to undergo reconstruction every 20 years, following the tradition of the {{ill|Jingū Shikinen Sengū|ja|式年遷宮|lt=Shikinen Sengū}} at the Ise Grand Shrine<ref name="sk0"/>. However, records of reconstruction ceased after an entry from December 8, 1340, which mentions an order to rebuild the shrine using rice tributes from Tajima Province<ref name="sk0"/>.

In 1663 (Kanbun 3), the shrine was restored by Grand Priest {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長}} in Yamaga Village, Okatani<ref name="sk0"/>. {{ill|Mikannagi Kiyonao|ja|御巫清直|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mikado Kiyonao|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q6537624}} later criticized this restoration site as inappropriate in his work ''Ninomiya Kansha Engaku Kō'', proposing that the original site was within Yamaga Village at the remains of the former {{ill|Yahashira Shrine|ja|八柱神社|lt=Yahashira Shrine}}, which had been merged in 1908 (Meiji 41)<ref>Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp.201–202</ref>.

The current location was established in 1876 (Meiji 9)<ref name="sk0"/>. The shrine building was reconstructed in 1922 (Taishō 11)<ref name="uy"/>.

== Rituals ==
On the 16th day of the 3rd lunar month, a ritual known as ''Miyatamori Shinji'' (宮田もり神事) is held, which is associated with {{ill|Kōshin|en|Kōshin|qid=Q3082157|lt=Kōshin belief}}<ref>Sakurai (1991): p.293</ref>.

During the {{ill|Kinensai|en|Kinen-sai|qid=Q118906710|lt=Kinen-sai}} (February), {{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭}} (June and December), {{ill|Kannamesai Festival|en|Kannamesai Festival|qid=Q11255045|lt=Kannamesai}} (October), and {{ill|Niiname-no-Matsuri|en|Niiname-no-Matsuri|qid=Q11501518|lt=Niiname-sai}} (November), rituals are conducted in front of the shrine. For the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭}} (January 1), {{ill|Genshi-sai|ja|元始祭}} (January), {{ill|Kenkoku Kinen no Hi|ja|建国記念祭}} (February 11), {{ill|Kazahi-no-Misai|ja|風日祈祭|2=ja|3=風日祈祭|qid=Q135524493|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fūhi no Sai|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135524493}} (May and August), and {{ill|The Emperor's Birthday|ja|天長祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenchō-sai|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天皇誕生日|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q72318}} (December 23), remote rituals are performed at the Gojōden of the Ise Grand Shrine<ref>Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp.200–201</ref>.

== Access ==
Near the shrine are the ruins of an ancient icehouse (氷室) associated with the {{ill|Saikū|en|Saikū|qid=Q150845|lt=Saikū}}<ref name="ic"/>. About 2.5 km from Kamo Shrine is the {{ill|Kamoshimo Shrine|ja|鴨下神社}}, which enshrines the same deity and is located within the same Shirota region<ref name="sk0"/>.

; By Public Transport
There are no nearby train stations or bus stops. From {{ill|Tamaru Station|en|Tamaru Station|qid=Q117533|lt=Tamaru Station}} on the {{ill|Sangū Line|en|Sangū Line|qid=Q872023|lt=JR Sangū Line}}, it is about a 50-minute walk (4.0 km) southwest, or about 53 minutes (4.3 km) south from {{ill|Tokida Station|en|Tokida Station|qid=Q7813584|lt=Sotojōda Station}}<ref name="ic"/>. From Yamaga village, a stone marker labeled "Kamo Shrine" leads through a bamboo grove, under a tunnel beneath the {{ill|Ise Expressway|en|Ise Expressway|qid=Q6079578|lt=Ise Expressway}}, and along a mountain path to the shrine<ref name="ic"/>. The distance from the marker to the shrine is about 1.1 km<ref>Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.63</ref>, taking around 20 minutes<ref name="gk"/>. There are forestry roads nearby, so caution is advised to avoid getting lost<ref name="ic"/>.

; By Car
From {{ill|Tamaki interchange|ja|玉城インターチェンジ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamaki Interchange|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11572465}} on the Ise Expressway, it takes about 6 minutes (2.1 km) to reach the stone marker for Kamo Shrine<ref name="gk"/>. The mountain path beyond the marker is for pedestrians only, and vehicles cannot pass through. However, there is a parking area near {{ill|Matoyama Park|ja|的山公園}}, which is accessible via a tunnel under the Ise Expressway. This route includes a paved mountain path, reducing the walking distance.
